If you are aiming for a doctorate or habilitation, the faculty is an important point of contact, as we are responsible for the procedures and the awarding of the academic degrees.
In the following we would like to inform you in particular about all formal questions relating to the doctorate - from the initial orientation, the declaration of intent to pursue a doctorate, the doctorate procedure to the publication of your dissertation.
In addition, you find below the contact details of the ombudsperson for doctoral candidates of the faculty who you can contact in case of problems or conflicts, and of the Center for Junior Scholars of TU Berlin.
If you are aiming for a habilitation, please contact the Faculty Service Center directly, we will be happy to advise you.

Steps towards a doctorate
To help ensure that your doctorate proposal is processed quickly, we kindly ask you to observe the following steps and information. The required forms can be found in the relevant chapters or under "Downloads".
Important: Please do make an appointment for submitting documents personally!
Expand all
Collapse all
1. General orientation
How can I do a doctorate at Faculty VI?
Please inform yourself first about the different ways to do a doctorate. Faculty VI does not offer any general, structured doctoral programs. It is therefore important to find a supervisor for your doctoral project on your own, according to your planned topic (see the list of all chairs of Faculty VI as well as chapter 2 below). In addition, please clarify the question of funding before starting a doctorate.
In addition, the TU Center for Junior Scholars has published a very helpful information brochure for international doctoral students which gives a good overview of the first steps towards a doctorate.
On which basis can I do a doctorate at Faculty VI?
The basis for completing a doctorate at Faculty VI are the joint doctoral regulations of TU Berlin including their first amendment and the implementing regulations of Faculty VI.
Familiarity with the details of the doctoral regulations and the implementing regulations of Faculty VI is assumed in the case of requests for advice!
At Faculty VI Planning Building Environment you can pursue one of the four types of doctoral degrees:
Doctor of Engineering Sciences (Dr.-Ing.),
Doctor of Natural Sciences (Dr. rer. nat.),
Doctor of Philosophy (Dr. phil.) or
Doctor of Economic Sciences (Dr. rer. oec.).
The doctoral degree awarded is determined in § 2 of the Doctoral Regulations:
“The focus of the dissertation depends on the doctoral degree: for Dr.-Ing., the focus is on an engineering science, for Dr. rer. nat., it is on a mathematical or natural science, for Dr. phil., the humanities or the social sciences, and for Dr. rer. oec., economics or business administration.”
2. Declaration of intent to pursue a doctorate
Once you have found a supervisor for your doctoral project, you officially register as a doctoral candidate at Faculty VI by notifying us of your intent to pursue a doctorate.
You do this by completing the relevant form (English or German version), signing the form and submitting it together with these additional documents:
Brief description / summary of the planned dissertation
Work and time schedule for completing the dissertation
Signed current CV
Certified copies of diplomas and certificates of university degrees (Bachelor and Master!) and transcripts (list of grades and subjects) pursuant to Section 3 of the Doctoral Regulations. Alternatively, you can arrange an on-site appointment to present the originals. For documents issued in languages other than German or English, certified translations are required.
Signed confirmation of supervision (sample)
Completed statistical data entry sheet.
Please note: we do only accept original signatures (wet ink on paper), not a scan of the signature! Please send us all documents either by post to the address below or make an appointment to hand in the documents in person at the doctoral office. Unfortunately, a purely digital submission is not sufficient.
Your doctoral project can only be supervised by one of the following persons who must be a member of Faculty VI of TU Berlin:
Full-time professor
university lecturer
junior professor
post-doctoral research group leader
permanently employed full-time non-scheduled professor.
In addition to the confirmation of supervision, you need to conclude a bilateral doctoral agreement with the supervisor detailing the nature and extent of the supervision. However, the Faculty Service Centre does not require this document for registration.
Once the documents have been submitted and approved, you will receive a confirmation letter of your intent to do a doctorate from the Dean. Only with this confirmation you can enrol at TU Berlin as the next step.
Please note: Doctoral candidates who are not employed at TU Berlin are obliged to enrol! Employed doctoral candidates have the choice. Enrolment does not take place via the Faculty Administration but via the Office of Student Affairs of TU Berlin.
3. Scientific Writing
Proper academic conduct is an essential component of a doctorate. It ensures that results are verifiable and reproducible, distinguishes one’s own ideas from those of others, and demonstrates, overall, that one is capable of conducting independent research.
For this reason, several institutes within Faculty VI established guidelines and rules on good academic practice for their doctoral candidates, which must be followed:
Regulations of the Institute of Applied Geosciences
Regulations of the Institute of Architecture
Regulations of the Institute of Sociology
Regulations of the Institute of Urban and Regional Planning
For doctoral candidates from institutes that have not established their own regulations yet, the regulations of the Institute of Architecture shall apply in accordance with a decision by the Faculty Council.
All regulations are based on the “Guidelines for Safeguarding Good Research Practice at TU Berlin” from 2023, which must also be observed.

4. Application for admission to the doctoral procedure / submission of the dissertation
Once you have completed your doctoral thesis, you can submit it and apply to be admitted to the doctoral procedure at the same time. You can download and fill out a German version of the relevant form or an English version.
Your application should include your preferred reviewers. You can also nominate who you would like to be chair of the doctoral committee. Please refer to the requirements stated in the doctoral regulations and in the implementing regulations of Faculty VI regarding this.
We recommend you to send the completed application form (including information on co-authorships) and the title page digitally to promotionen@fak6.tu-berlin.de in advance in order to obtain initial feedback before printing. However, the submission of your dissertation and of the final application including all documents can only be done either by post or in person. Please note the following:
If you send the package by post, please always notify us at promotionen@fak6.tu-berlin.de and provide us with the tracking number! Otherwise, we cannot guarantee successful delivery. The correct and complete postal address is:
Technische Universität Berlin
Faculty VI, Doctorates
Secr. A1, Rooms 101–110
Straße des 17. Juni 152
10623 Berlin
GERMANY
If you hand in the package in person, please make an appointment in advance!
In addition to the completed and signed form, you should also submit the following documents to the Faculty Administration:
Printed copies of your completed dissertation:
Please note the specifications for the layout of the title page (which are different from those of the title page for the later publication!).
Please do not include an acknowledgement at this stage of the procedure.
However, include a declaration of authorship as well as a summary in English and German in each copy.
If you conducted interviews for your dissertation, an additional, adapted declaration must also be included in each copy.
The number of copies you are required to submit depends on the number of reviewers you wish to have. You are also required to submit two additional copies for the chair of the doctoral committee and the Faculty Service Center.
An electronic copy of the dissertation in PDF format on as USB stick
CV in tabular form (updated if necessary) on paper with original signature
A complete list of all publications
If not previously submitted: Certified copies of diplomas and certificates of all university degrees and transcripts (list of grades and subjects) or simple copies upon presentation of original documents (as well as certified translations, if applicable)
If not previously submitted: Completed statistical data entry sheet
Additional documents if you have prior publications or if you are submitting a cumulative dissertation (see the check list of the form and the implementing regulations of Faculty VI). Please note the University Library's copyright notices at this point.
An application for inspection of the assessments before the scientific debate and confidentiality agreement, if applicable (see also chapter 4 below).
Important: The dissertation must later be published as it was submitted (see chapter 5 for exceptions). Revisions, shortenings etc. are then no longer possible. Please bear this in mind when completing your dissertation.
NEW: In accordance with a decision by the Faculty Council, every tenth dissertation submitted will be checked with plagiarism software. Please clarify any uncertainties and questions regarding correct scientific writing with your supervisor BEFORE the submission.
5. Scientific defense
After the opening of the doctoral procedure and the appointment of the doctoral committee by the dean, the reviewers prepare their reviews usually within three months.The date for the scientific defense can only be set once all reviews have been received by the faculty administration. The chairperson of the doctoral committee is responsible for coordinating the date and organising the defense. The Faculty Service Center requires at least three weeks between receipt of the reviews and the date of the scientific defense in order to be able to meet all specified deadlines.
The scientific defense is open to the university public and takes place in the presence of the doctoral candidate and all members of the doctoral committee. A digital participation of the external reviewers is possible and preferred.
The scientific defense is divided into two parts:
Presentation by the doctoral candidate about the dissertation (approx. 30 minutes)
Discussion with the reviewers about the subject discipline of the dissertation (approx. 60 minutes).
After having successfully passed the scientific defense, the candidate is issued with a provisional certificate.
Inspection of the reviews
According to § 8 (1) of the doctoral regulations, doctoral candidates of Faculty VI are allowed to inspect the assessments before the scientific defense, provided that the supervisor belongs to one of the following institutes of Faculty VI (first membership):
Institute of Architecture
Institute of Landscape Architecture and Environmental Planning
Institute of Ecology
Institute of Sociology
Institute of Urban and Regional Planning
For this purpose, an application for inspection with a confidentiality agreement can be submitted. Provided that this application is submitted in time and signed in the original, the Faculty Service Center will send the reviews (without grades and requirements) to the doctoral candidate by email 14 days before the scientific defense.
6. Publication and Handing over of the certificate
After the completion your scientific defense, you are required to publish your dissertation within twelve months pursuant to Section 9 of the Doctoral Regulations (extension only in exceptional cases upon request).
Therefore, you contact the Dissertation Office of the University Library of TU Berlin, which provides various options for fulfilling this publication obligation:
Online publication in DepositOnce (checklist)
Submission of 15 printed copies as standard dissertation copies (checklist)
Submission of three publication copies (checklist, for possible changes by the publishing house, please see the implementing regulations of Faculty VI, too)
Please note the following when publishing:
You must publish the version of your dissertation approved by the doctoral committee. This means that the dissertation must be published 1:1 as it was submitted. Exceptions to this are:
Possible requirements of the doctoral committee, which will be communicated to you by the Faculty Service Center after the scientific defense and which must be incorporated.
Minor formal corrections (spelling or formatting errors) as well as changes with regard to the formatting requirements of the UB Dissertation Office, among others:
The title page, which will be different for publication than for submission. Please note the information of the UB Dissertation Office concerning this aspect.
An acknowledgement, which can be included now.
In case of a thesis by publication (cumulative dissertation), please consider additional information including copyright notices.
After publication, you will receive a confirmation of receipt (confirmation of publication) from the UB dissertation office, a copy of which is usually sent to the faculty administration.
If the doctoral committee imposed requirements, the Faculty Service Center needs a confirmation from the doctoral committee about the successfully incorporated changes. In addition, you must submit a printed copy of the final, published dissertation to the Faculty Service Center.
Then, the doctoral certificate can be handed over to you or sent to your postal address by registered mail. Please make an appointment in advance if you wish to collect it in person! If you wish to have it sent to you, please check whether the postal address given in your application for the opening the doctoral procedure is still the current address or inform us of an alternative address.

If necessary, you can also schedule a personal, telephone, or online consultation by email. Please include your contact information and a detailed description of your inquiry.
Email
Ombudsperson for Doctoral Candidates
Doctoral candidates who need advice with problems or conflicts can contact the ombudsperson for doctoral candidates ("Vertrauensperson für Promovierende") of faculty VI. All requests are treated confidentially and any further action is only taken in agreement with the candidate.
Please note: the ombudsperson is not responsible for formal or administrative questions. Such issues are dealt with by the Faculty Service Center (see above).
